title: unified-tool-executor: idempotent-parallel-calls + streaming hooks + OpenAI-compat fallback
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers asked for clearer semantics around parallel tool/function calls, deterministic result injection, and safe retries when side effects exist. This PR introduces a unified executor API that 1) provides an idempotency token model for speculative parallel tool execution, 2) surfaces streaming hooks so callers can receive partial tool outputs and executor events, 3) standardizes a provenance envelope for injected tool results so downstream structured-output and streaming consumers can reconcile origins, and 4) adds an OpenAI-compat adapter fallback path that preserves the new semantics for existing integrations. Implementation notes and tradeoffs are described below. -- Design: the executor exposes a new ExecuteTools RPC and HTTP endpoint that accepts a call_graph with per-tool metadata: idempotency_token, expected_effects (none|read|write), timeout_ms, max_retries, and inject_strategy (ordered|merge-by-key|first-responder). The executor may run tools in parallel when allowed by declared dependencies. Each tool result is wrapped in a provenance envelope {tool_id, run_id, attempt, token, produced_stream_checkpoint} which is encoded as metadata in both streaming frames and final JSON injection. Streams emit three event types: EXECUTOR_EVENT (scheduler decisions), TOOL_FRAME (partial stdout/kvs), and INJECTION_POINT (final harmonized result). -- Retry semantics: retries are only attempted for tools where expected_effects != "write" unless the caller explicitly requests at-least-once and supplies a compensating idempotency_token. Retries attach a monotonic attempt number in the provenance envelope; the executor provides a deterministic merging policy for duplicate keys and documents the fallback order for inject_strategy. -- OpenAI compat: added openai_adapter shim that accepts function_call style requests and maps them to call_graph entries. For streaming function_call flows we preserve event ordering by replaying TOOL_FRAME events as chunked function call payloads and final INJECTION_POINT as the function result. This keeps compatibility with existing SDKs while improving observability. -- Backwards compatibility: default behavior is conservative: existing routes using single-tool invocation see no behavior change. The new endpoint is opt-in. -- Tests and rollout: added unit tests for merge policies and provenance envelopes, integration tests that drive parallelism across the runtime on CPU and GPU runners, and an end-to-end smoke test that verifies OpenAI-compat streaming function_call mapping. We will roll out behind a feature flag and enable Canary in the perf-canary infra for 48 hours before full rollout. -- Migration notes: SDKs are updated with new ergonomic helpers. Calls without idempotency_token get a generated token but are subject to default conservative retry rules. -- Links: Linear ENG-3417, ENG-3522.
